data.name: Grand Teton Scenic Float - Private Tour
data.headline: 2.5 Hours • Ages 5+ (50lbs+) • Season: May-September
data.description:
Discover the beauty of Grand Teton National Park on a serene scenic float down the wild and scenic Snake River. 

This two-hour guided experience with Solitude Float Trips offers sweeping views of the Teton Range and opportunities to spot wildlife such as moose, elk, and bald eagles as you float. With a knowledgeable guide at the oars, you’ll enjoy a calm, informative journey through Jackson Hole’s pristine braided river corridor. 

Ideal for families, couples, and nature lovers, this float trip is a memorable way to explore the heart of the Tetons.

## Waitlist
Is the trip you were hoping for not available online?  Enter your details in our waitlist so we can check availability for you and either find you an alternative, or find you a guide!  After you enter your details, we will get to work, looking at your options for the day.  We will reach out and provide you with some tours to choose from that you can reserve right away.

data.cancellation_notes:
*For public tours or private tours with 12 guests or less (excluding custom tours):*
We have a **48-hour cancellation policy.** Cancellations made at least 48 hours prior to departure will receive a full refund. Within 48 hours, bookings are non-refundable.

*For private tours, custom tours, and large groups of 12+ guests:*
We have a **30-day cancellation policy.** Cancellations made at least 30 days prior to departure will receive a refund, minus a 5% fee. Within 30 days, bookings are non-refundable.

**We highly recommend obtaining travel insurance before your departure to protect you from incurring any costs associated with unforeseen circumstances that prevent you from joining us.**

##What to Wear
Make sure to dress in layers that are appropriate for the weather conditions on the day of your tour.  Our days can start out cool and end up warm in the summer months, and the mountain weather is always variable, so come prepared with layers you can add or remove as needed to keep yourself comfortable.  Be sure to pack your rain jacket in your daypack, just in case.  

#Before Arrival
Please take time to [read our waiver](https://grand-teton-scenic-floats.com/risk-agreement/)  that you will be required to sign prior to departure.

*A Reminder: Please take time to review the cancellation policy.  Due to limited seating, we strictly adhere to the stated policy.*

data.special_requirements:
All guests must be properly fitted in one of our USCG Approved Personal Floatation Devices (life jacket) in order to participate in a float trip. This generally means adult guests must weigh between 90-260lbs with a chest size not to exceed 56 inches.  

For children, they must weigh at least 50lbs to fit into an approved life jacket suitable for this stretch of river.  

If you do not meet these requirements, please reach out to our office directly to review your options.
data.restrictions:
**Children**
In order to participate in the scenic float, your child must be at least five years old and weigh at least 50 pounds. This will ensure that they are properly fitted for a personal flotation device (PFD or life jacket).  Additionally, consider your child’s attention span as the trip is about two hours in duration (2.5 counting shuttle) with no stops (or restroom breaks) on the river.

**Older Adults**
We welcome older adults to participate in our scenic floats. If you have special concerns it might be best for you to call the office to describe your specific situation as a person must be able to self-rescue in the unlikely event that it should become necessary.

While a scenic float is not necessarily an athletic activity per se, some agility and mobility is required. Drivers and guides can offer some assistance to you, but you must be fundamentally responsible for yourself throughout the course of the trip.

Specifically, you will be transported in a 15-passenger van, which will require you to step up into the van and possibly climb into the back, if necessary.  You will ride in the van for a short shuttle (15-20 mins) to the launch.  At the launch, you will need to be able to climb three steps onto the trailer we use for a dock.  Once on the trailer, you will walk approximately 16 feet to the raft where you will be required to step down into the raft (approximately 18-20 inches).  Once on the raft, you will sit on the tube of the raft.  Please note there is no cover on the raft for shade or solid back support.  When you disembark, you will be asked to walk on uneven ground up a river bank approximately 5 yards until you reach flat pavement.  You are then approximately 100 yards from where your car is parked.  The landing area changes depending on the time of year, with there being little room to maneuver when the water is high (typically May – July).

Please note it is very difficult for our office staff to assess your particular situation from afar. We ask that you reflect upon these requirements honestly and determine for yourself if you believe you are capable of participating in this activity.
